update.effect: Run the detected native updater between lanes in a detached one-shot worker scheduled by quota events. false opts out; {command: [program, argument, ...]} overrides the updater directly without a shell.

update_timeout_seconds.effect: Maximum native updater duration in the detached worker. Timeout kills the updater process group and records failure. Updater descendants retain the exclusive lease until exit, including descendants that leave the group.

update_interval_seconds.effect: Minimum time between update attempts, checked on existing housekeeping events. Failed and interrupted attempts and result-write errors wait the same interval.

history_max_bytes.effect: Disk cap for each account's quota history under quota/history/. Readings go to a current file that rotates to one predecessor at half the cap, so the pair never exceeds it and the newest reading is always kept.

directories.effect: Optional list of absolute config directories, in addition to directory, that are signed into the same account, for example ~/.claude-anese and ~/.claude. At most 8. Schema only: nothing reads it yet; native session ingest will use it to attribute sessions to the account.

plans.form: array of tables, any number of entries

fields.name: Plan label, for example max_5x. At most 64 characters.
fields.price: Price per month in currency; 0 or more, 0 for a free plan.
fields.currency: Three capital letters (ISO 4217). USD when omitted. No conversion is applied.
fields.notional_usd: Optional list-price value in USD of a free or discounted plan, for example 20 for a student plan priced 0.
fields.effective_from: First day the price applies, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC).

plans.effect: Prices over time for the account. The entry with the latest effective_from on or before a reading applies to it, and quota history --json shows it as plan_price, with price and notional_usd. Dates must differ within an account; unknown keys, negative or non-finite prices and bad dates refuse the config. This is not the detected plan label, which comes from the provider or the account's plan option.

max_concurrent_builds.effect: Maximum active worktree-write lanes across the host.

cargo_build_jobs.default: Half the available cores, at least 1
cargo_build_jobs.effect: Default CARGO_BUILD_JOBS for lanes; an inherited value takes precedence.

cargo_incremental.effect: CARGO_INCREMENTAL for lanes. Incremental sessions grow a lane's target without bound and are rarely reused; a value already in the lane environment takes precedence.

cargo_debug.allowed: none, line-directives-only, line-tables-only, limited, full, 0, 1, 2, true or false
cargo_debug.effect: CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG for lanes. Line tables keep backtraces at a fraction of the size of full debug information; a value already in the lane environment takes precedence.

build_dir_max_bytes.effect: Cap on the allocated bytes of all Cargo profile directories in lane caches, idle and busy alike. Collection removes idle directories, least recently used first, after a lane settles, when admission finds the disk below gc.free_floor, and in `provenant gc`; a directory whose Cargo locks are held is never removed. When busy directories alone exceed the cap, every eligible idle directory is removed and the total stays over.

build_dir_grace_seconds.effect: A profile directory whose newest file or directory modification is within this many seconds is never removed, even when its Cargo locks are free: test and run binaries execute after Cargo drops its locks, and Cargo may be opening its lock files. Zero removes the protection. It protects only recently written directories: a test or run binary that runs longer than the grace without writing under target/ is unprotected unless a Cargo lock is still held.

build_dir_survey_interval_seconds.effect: Settlement-triggered collection walks the lane caches at most this often, unless free space is below gc.free_floor or the last walk found the total within 10% of the cap. While free space stays below the floor, every settlement walks. Zero walks on every settlement.

domains.routing.capacity_cooldown_second.effect: Avoid a model and account in automatic draws for this many seconds after a provider capacity error. Zero disables new cooldowns.
domains.routing.capacity_cooldown_second.trade_off: Longer cooldowns reduce repeated capacity errors but keep affected models out of automatic draws for longer.

usage.project_attribution.effect: Include the existing project identifier in local usage events.
usage.project_attribution.trade_off: Off keeps project identity out of usage logs; on makes project-level usage visible to anyone who can read them.

fabric.accept_handoff.effect: Let a Fabric peer start a Claude session on this host through a session hand-off.
fabric.accept_handoff.trade_off: Off refuses every hand-off with HANDOFF_DISABLED; on lets a peer open an unconfined session under a registered account.

chair.auto_switch.effect: Allow the Claude UserPromptSubmit hook to checkpoint and switch accounts at the quota threshold.
chair.auto_switch.trade_off: Off keeps switching manual; on opens a new chair pane when an explicitly allowed account has headroom.

chair.switch_threshold.effect: Switch when either the five-hour or weekly cached Claude usage reaches this percentage.
chair.switch_threshold.trade_off: Lower switches sooner; higher leaves less headroom for the handoff.

chair.switch_accounts.effect: Ordered registered Claude account labels allowed as switch targets; empty allows none.
chair.switch_accounts.trade_off: An explicit list controls which signed-in accounts may receive the chair.

lanes.silence_seconds.effect: Mark a provider observation silent after this many seconds without output or CPU progress; never kill it for silence.
lanes.silence_seconds.trade_off: Lower marks silence sooner; the process census and observation cadence stays unchanged.

lanes.max_concurrency.effect: Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when any lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins.
lanes.max_concurrency.trade_off: Lower paces quota and memory and lengthens wall time; total tokens are unchanged.

lanes.max_concurrency_read_only.effect: Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when no lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. A lanes.max_concurrency you set yourself also caps it unless you set this knob too. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins.
lanes.max_concurrency_read_only.trade_off: Lower paces quota and memory and lengthens wall time; total tokens are unchanged. Read-only lanes start 2 s apart whatever this value.

lanes.max_depth.effect: Maximum nested lane depth, including the first dispatched lane.
lanes.max_depth.trade_off: Lower limits delegation chains; higher permits deeper nested work.

lanes.publish.effect: Let worktree-write lanes with open network read gh configuration, push branches and open pull requests.
lanes.publish.trade_off: Off keeps publishing with the chair; on exposes the existing gh login read-only to the writer lane.

review.extra_reviewers.effect: Independent reviews added on top of the HARNESS.md ladder minimum for the tier.
review.extra_reviewers.trade_off: Each extra review costs one reviewer lane and adjudication time for wider defect coverage.

review.cross_family.effect: prefer: a blocked cross-family leg is replaced by a same-family reviewer through another lens, as the ladder allows. require: wait for, or reroute to, another family instead.
review.cross_family.trade_off: require keeps decorrelated review at the price of waiting on quota or outages.

review.rereview_scope.effect: After a repair, re-review only the repair delta, or the whole change again.
review.rereview_scope.trade_off: full catches interactions between the repair and untouched code at roughly the cost of the first review.

review.polish.effect: auto: one behaviour-preserving polish lane before review when the diff exceeds about 300 lines or touches more than one crate or package. always: every change. off: never.
review.polish.trade_off: Polish costs one writer lane per qualifying change for a simpler diff and shorter review.

balanced.description: Today's behaviour: every knob at its registry default.

economy.description: Less usage per task, accepting slower runs and no polish lane.

rigorous.description: Correctness first: more independent review, full re-review.
